## The tracer flux positivity limiter (`equation-of-state/limiter`) {#sec-ch08-theta}

### Summary

This is the only mechanism in snapy that *guarantees* anything about positivity, and it guarantees it for tracers
alone. For each cell and species it computes the largest uniform scaling of that cell's outgoing fluxes that cannot
drain it below zero in one forward-Euler step. It then applies the factor of the donor cell to every face. It runs
inside the stage operator of @sec-ch04-divergence, after the seam averaging of @sec-ch04-seam and before the flux
divergence.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Scale each face's tracer flux by the factor of the cell it drains, @eq-ch08-theta-def, so no cell is emptied past zero.

**Data.** In: the tracer rows of `hydro_u`, the three face fluxes, $\Delta t$. Out: the fluxes scaled in place, and a census.

**Placement.** In `HydroImpl::forward`, after the seam averaging and before the flux divergence, every stage.

**Activation.** `equation-of-state/limiter: true`, or any face-flux covariance row on (the default); tracer rows present.

**Guarantee / limits.** $u_i + \Delta t\,\Delta u_i \ge 0$ per stage, explicit transport only; exactly conservative; nothing for density or pressure.

**Evidence.** `[C1]`, `[C2]`, `[C3]`, `[C5]`, `[C7]` of this chapter's check; the ctests of @tbl-ch08-theta-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathrm{out}_i$ is what leaves cell $i$ per unit time [units of $u$ times volume per time]. $\Theta_i$
is the dimensionless factor of cell $i$, never above 1. $u_i$, $V_i$, $A_f F_f$ and $\Delta t$ are the tracer density,
the cell volume, a face area times its normal flux, and the stage step of @sec-ch04-divergence.

### Derivation

Charge each cell for what leaves it. Summing the outgoing part of $AF$ over the cell's faces,

$$
\mathrm{out}_i = \sum_{f} \max(\pm A_f F_f,\, 0),\qquad
\Theta_i = \min\!\left(1,\ \frac{u_i V_i}{\Delta t\,\mathrm{out}_i}\right),
$$ {#eq-ch08-theta-def}

with the sign chosen so that only genuinely outgoing contributions count: inflow is not charged. Here $u_i$ is the
cell's tracer density, $V_i$ its volume, $A_f F_f$ a face area times its normal flux, and $\Delta t$ the stage time
step, all as defined in @sec-ch04-divergence. This section defines the other two. $\mathrm{out}_i$ is what leaves the
cell per unit time, in units of $u$ times volume per time, and $\Theta_i$, a dimensionless factor never greater than
1. @eq-ch08-theta-def is `flux_positivity_theta` ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}),
with the outgoing sum built from `relu` ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}). Applying
$\Theta$ of the donor cell to every face then gives $u_i + \Delta t\,\Delta u_i \ge 0$ cell by cell.

`[C1]` checks the guarantee on the state rather than on the formula. Over four thousand random flux
fields the unlimited update drives some cell negative in every one, worst $-5.879$; the limited update
never does, worst exactly $0$. The check computes the divergence independently of the limiter, so it
measures the result and not the construction.

Two properties are worth separating, because they are easy to conflate and the chapter is more useful
if they are kept apart.

*Where the limiter acts.* `[C2]` finds that every one of the $25\,974$ cells that can afford their outflow keeps
$\Theta = 1$ bitwise. No cell which cannot afford it was left unlimited. The scheme is therefore not a smoothing: away
from depletion the high-order flux passes through untouched.

*Why it conserves.* The conservation does **not** come from the donor rule. It comes from both cells of a face seeing
one number, so that the face cancels when the divergence is summed. `[C3]` separates these: on a closed block the
limited tendency sums to $1.7\times10^{-16}$ of the flux scale. A per-cell limiter, in which each cell scales only its
own outflow and its neighbour does not agree, leaks $8.5\times10^{-1}$. Any single factor per face telescopes; the
donor rule is what buys positivity, and `[C7]` checks that rule separately on forty-six thousand faces.

The step is limited at the full $\Delta t$ even inside a multi-stage integrator, and that is sound because of how the
shipped integrators are built. `[C5]` reads their weights rather than assuming them. Each stage is
$w_0 U^n + w_1(U + \alpha_{\mathrm{st}}\,\Delta U)$ with $w_0 + w_1 = 1$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{st}} = w_2/w_1 \le 1$, a convex combination of a
state already known non-negative and a damped full-step Euler update.

The factors are built by `flux_positivity_theta` at {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}.
The outgoing sum is accumulated over exactly the faces the divergence will consume, with a pair of rectified terms per
direction at `slice` ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}). So the limiter and the
divergence cannot disagree about which face drains which cell.

Two details of that function matter to a reader. The available mass stops a little short of zero, at `margin`
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}), because an exact-zero target rounds negative; that
margin is @sec-ch08-roundoff. And ghost cells are given $\Theta = 1$ here, because their outflow is never accumulated.
The caller must fill the ghost layer the way conserved variables are filled before scaling. Otherwise the two ranks
sharing a face would apply different factors and conservation would fail.

The scaling is `flux_positivity_scale_` at {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_scale_ >}}, which
selects the donor per face with a `where` on the sign of the flux. The call site is `narrow`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), which also keeps the census that @sec-ch08-roundoff
describes. The ghost fill it depends on follows at `pmb`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), a raw copy that is never interpolated because an
interpolated ghost is not the neighbour's factor.

**The covariance gate.** The face-flux covariance rows of @sec-ch04-fluxcov can export tracer that a cell does not
hold. So the stage runs this limiter whenever they are on, not only when `limiter` is set. The condition is
`cov2 || cov3` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), where `cov2`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) and `cov3`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) record that a covariance row was added on the $x_2$ or
$x_3$ faces. The passive scalars have the same gate (@sec-ch08-scalar). The gate binds only where the covariance is on
and the limiter is off. With either the limiter on or the covariance off the stage limits exactly as it would without
it. What the gate is worth is measured on the six-panel moist deck of `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_moist.py`,
covariance on, limiter off, 40 cycles. The minimum vapour is $-2.2\times10^{-10}$ with the gate suppressed against 0
with it. Kintera's negative-concentration warnings 1474 against 0. The species drift that remains in that arm,
$2.4\times10^{-10}$ and the same as in the limited arm, is the panel-seam leak of @sec-ch04-fluxcov, not a failure of
the gate.[^ch08-gate-numbers]

**Why the donor factor, and what it costs.** Four facts of the code and two bounds.

1. The outgoing sum is accumulated over exactly the faces the divergence consumes, as a rectified pair per direction
   ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}). So the limiter and the divergence agree about
   which face drains which cell.
2. The available mass is $(1 - 4096\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m})\,\max(u_i, 0)\,V_i$, not $u_i V_i$: an exact-zero target rounds
   negative, so a margin of 4096 ulp is kept (@sec-ch08-roundoff). The fraction left behind is $9.1\times10^{-13}$ in
   double precision and $4.9\times10^{-4}$ in single.
3. Both cells of a face use one factor, so the scaled flux telescopes when the divergence is summed. The only error is
   the rounding of that sum, at most $(n_f - 1)\,\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ times the sum of the face magnitudes over
   $n_f$ faces; `[C3]` measures $1.7\times10^{-16}$ of the flux scale.
4. The ghost factors are a raw copy, never interpolated ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):
   the donor of a seam face is the neighbour's edge cell, and an interpolated ghost is not its factor.

: Code map of the tracer flux positivity limiter. {#tbl-ch08-theta-code}

**How to use it.** Turn the limiter on in the card; it also turns on the floors of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter and
@sec-ch08-reconfloors ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}):

```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state:
    limiter: true   # default false
```

With the face-flux covariance on, which is the default, the limiter runs even with `limiter: false`; the
unlimited scheme needs `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=0` in the environment as well. Refused: nothing of its own; the
limiter is skipped when there are no tracer rows. The factor is these lines of `flux_positivity_theta`
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}):

```cpp
  double margin = kPositivityRoundoffUlp * machine_epsilon(u.scalar_type());
  auto avail = u.relu() * pcoord->cell_volume() * (1. - margin);
  auto drain = out.mul_(dt);
  if (drain_out) *drain_out = drain;
  return torch::where(drain > 0.,
                      (avail / drain.clamp_min(1e-300)).clamp_max(1.0),
                      torch::ones_like(u));
```

`avail` is the mass the cell can afford, `drain` the mass it would lose unlimited, and the ratio is clamped at one. A
cell that drains nothing keeps the factor one. The gate in the stage is
`if ((options->eos()->limiter() || cov2 || cov3) && ny > 0)`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

: Tests of the tracer flux positivity limiter. {#tbl-ch08-theta-tests}

Because the covariance defaults on and turns this limiter on with it, the arms that mean to run unlimited set
`SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=0`. The limiter-off arms of `test_flux_positivity_carry` ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}) and
`test_flux_positivity_python` ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}) do so. The first withholds no flux (`limited` = 0)
and the second's unlimited base arm stays positive with drifts at $4\times10^{-16}$. A second arm of the six-panel
test, `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_cov_off` ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}), keeps the unlimited base arm
covered with the covariance off.[^ch08-gate-arms] No test asserts the minimum-vapour and warning counts quoted above;
they are **missing evidence** at a pinned sha.

The chapter's check is a numpy port of the factor and the donor rule on random flux fields; it imports no
snapy.[^ch08-theta-run] `[C1]`: over 4000 random fields the unlimited update goes negative in every one, worst
$-5.879$, and the limited update never does, worst exactly $0$. `[C2]`: all $25\,974$ cells that can afford
their outflow keep $\Theta = 1$ bitwise, and no cell that cannot was left unlimited. `[C3]`: on a closed block
the limited tendency sums to $1.7\times10^{-16}$ of the flux scale, while a per-cell limiter leaks
$8.5\times10^{-1}$. `[C5]`: every shipped integrator forms a stage as $w_0 U^n + w_1(U + \alpha_{\mathrm{st}}\,\Delta U)$
with $\alpha_{\mathrm{st}} \le 1$. `[C7]`: $46\,000$ interior faces follow the donor rule with no mismatch. The ctests named
above have not been run for this report at the pin: **pending a pinned ctest run**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Tracers only. Nothing here keeps dry density or pressure positive; those have floors
  (@sec-ch08-eoslimiter) and a redo detector (@sec-ch08-redo), and neither is a guarantee.
- `limiter: false` does not give the unlimited scheme while the covariance is on (the default); only
  `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=0` together with `limiter: false` does.
- The guarantee is per stage, for transport only. A source term, a sedimentation flux added after the
  limiter, or the implicit solve can still drive a tracer negative.
:::

1. **The ghost fill is a precondition, not a check.** If a caller scales before filling $\Theta$'s ghost layer, the
   two ranks of a seam face apply different factors. Conservation then breaks silently. The code says so in its
   header; nothing asserts it at runtime.
2. **Hypothesis, not measured here.** That limiting at the full $\Delta t$ is enough for the multi-stage update rests
   on the convex-combination argument `[C5]` verifies for the shipped weights. It is an argument about the weights,
   not a measurement of a multi-stage run; no check in this chapter integrates a full Runge-Kutta step.
